note: Berlin institutions that exist twice because the city was split. Coordinates geocoded from OpenStreetMap Nominatim on 28 August 2026. Sector polygons derived from the repo's east-west-1989 dataset.

west.name: Funkturm
west.fact: 126 m platform, Tuesday to Sunday 11:00 to 21:00, out at the Messe grounds.

east.name: Fernsehturm
east.fact: 203 m deck, open every day, straight up from Alexanderplatz.

pairs.verdict: Take the Fernsehturm if you want to look at the centre. Take the Funkturm if you want to look at the Fernsehturm, from a platform with almost nobody on it.

west.name: Zoo Berlin
west.fact: Germany's oldest zoo, about 33 hectares, five minutes from Bahnhof Zoo.

east.name: Tierpark
east.fact: Built by the GDR when the Zoo ended up in the west. Roughly five times the size, in a Lenne park.

pairs.verdict: Zoo Berlin if your day is short and already in the west. Tierpark if you want to walk in a park that happens to have animals in it.

west.name: Deutsche Oper
west.fact: Opened six weeks after the Wall went up, as West Berlin's only opera house.

east.name: Staatsoper
east.fact: The royal house, on the boulevard, rebuilt after the war and again after 2010.

pairs.verdict: Staatsoper for the gilded room and the walk home past the Dom. Deutsche Oper for cheaper seats and a hall that hides nothing behind decoration.

west.name: Philharmonie
west.fact: Built a few hundred metres from the Wall, with the orchestra in the middle of the room.

east.name: Konzerthaus
east.fact: Schinkel's theatre, rebuilt from a wartime ruin and reopened as a concert hall in October 1984.

pairs.verdict: Philharmonie if you care how a concert hall can sound. Konzerthaus if you want the room and the square it stands on.

west.name: Haus Potsdamer Strasse
west.fact: The terraced reading landscape from Wings of Desire. Same architect as the Philharmonie next door.

east.name: Haus Unter den Linden
east.fact: The old Prussian library, with a glass reading cube dropped into the bombed courtyard.

pairs.verdict: One library, two houses, because the collection was split and never fully put back. Potsdamer Strasse is the one worth walking into if you like buildings.

west.name: Planetarium am Insulaner
west.fact: Sits on a hill made of war rubble, next to an open-air pool.

east.name: Zeiss-Grossplanetarium
east.fact: One of the last big GDR buildings, put up for Berlin's 750th birthday. 23 m inner dome.

pairs.verdict: The Zeiss dome in Prenzlauer Berg is the bigger show and the easier trip. The Insulaner is the one you go to for the hill it stands on.

west.name: Rathaus Schoeneberg
west.fact: Kennedy said Ich bin ein Berliner from this balcony in 1963. The Freedom Bell in the tower rings at noon.

east.name: Rotes Rathaus
east.sub: Seat of the mayor again since 1991
east.fact: The red brick city hall behind the Neptune Fountain, back in charge of the whole city.

pairs.verdict: Rotes Rathaus is on your way anywhere in the centre. Schoeneberg is the one to plan for, and to arrive at just before twelve.

west.name: Kulturforum
west.fact: Where the western half of the old Prussian collections went. Nefertiti was out here until 2009.

east.name: Museum Island
east.fact: The eastern half stayed on the island, including the Pergamon collections.

pairs.verdict: Museum Island first, always. The Kulturforum is where you go on the second visit, when the island has stopped being the only thing you know about.

west.name: Bahnhof Zoo
west.fact: Every train into West Berlin ended here.

east.name: Ostbahnhof
east.fact: East Berlin's main station, and it carried the name Hauptbahnhof for eleven years.

now.name: Berlin Hauptbahnhof
now.fact: Opened in May 2006 on empty land between the two, and took the long-distance trains off both.

pairs.verdict: Settled. Book to Hauptbahnhof unless your hotel is genuinely closer to one of the old two.

west.name: Tegel
west.fact: The hexagon where you walked from the taxi to the gate in a minute. Tempelhof, also in the west, closed in 2008.

east.name: Schoenefeld
east.sub: East Berlin's airport, outside the city
east.fact: The GDR's airport was not even inside Berlin. It kept going as BER's Terminal 5 until it closed for good in 2022.

now.name: BER
now.fact: Opened on the Schoenefeld site on 31 October 2020. One airport, in the far south east.

pairs.verdict: Settled, and not in your favour: the surviving airport is the far one. Allow the full hour back into town.

west.name: Freie Universitaet
west.fact: Started by students who had been thrown out of the old university in the Soviet sector.

east.name: Humboldt-Universitaet
east.fact: The original, opposite the Staatsoper, with the second-hand book stalls out front.

pairs.verdict: Humboldt is a five second stop on any walk down Unter den Linden. The FU is a genuine trip to Dahlem, worth it only if Sixties campus architecture is your thing.
